status: Cargo's detail spec: the bay with its sealed crates (the whole), one crate opening (the arrival), the report card, and the rack the pods land in, handed to Pods. Wireframes 17-cargo-bay.svg to 17d-cargo-nav.svg
note: Rectangles are [x, y, w, h] in screen pixels; `at` offsets are from the region's own origin. The stage is the frame's (0, 40, 1024, 522); the top bar and the bottom line are the frame's.
stateRule: bay: the whole, the crates sealed in the bay (or none). opening: from ✓ Open the bay until the last crate has opened, one crate at a time, input held (events.opening). report: from the last crate's end until the next press, then bay, empty. A region with `inStates` exists only in those states

conditions.away: the Companion is not in the Caddy: no walk crates; the bay is shut unless a sitting crate is in it, and a ready sitting crate opens as docked
conditions.docked: the bay is open: one sealed crate per crate the Companion brought, at most three, or none

states.shut: away: the bay's lid across the inside
states.open: docked: the inside, the crates on its floor

crates.order: left to right, the order they open; places with no crate show the bay's floor
crates.overflow: more than three crates (developer only): the first three in bayCrates order show, walk crates first; no others are drawn; the context line counts all

sitting.places: from the right: the first at 704, a second at 384; walk crates fill from the left; at most three show, walk crates first

lamp.rule: under its crate, at (place.x + 122, 304): the rows lit from the bottom, floor(10 × crateLamp) in sky, the rest hairline; full only when ready

sitting.opens: a ready sitting crate opens in Cargo after the walk crates, in the same sequence, docked or away; its ribbon is strings.ribbon.sitting. It gets no row on the report; when only sitting crates opened, no report card shows and the bay shows at the end
sitting.revealNote: what the opened sitting crate shows (its portrait's reveal) is not designed yet (station-layouts.md, Not designed yet); until it is, a build leaves sitting crates out of the bay

waiting.when: pods wait in the bay for a free well

pod.note: the collection class, as Pods' collection draws it, rendered at 88×112

rack.rule: the six places of the rack, the same pods in the same order as Pods' collection: an empty well, or its pod; a pod still travelling leaves its well empty until it lands

pods.more: pods numbered i from 0 in well order; 0, 1, 2 stand left, middle, right; pod i ≥ 3 appears in the middle place as a cut at 1200 + 150·(i−1) and travels from there at 1200 + 150·i; a pod with no free well stays and no later pod appears; developer crates only (play has at most 3)

travel.from: its place in the open crate
travel.path: a straight line, whole pixels, eased in and out; nothing is scaled; a pod never leaves this rectangle
travel.ease: in-out: p = min(1000, t·1000/600); e = p·p·(3000 − 2p)/1000000 (64-bit); pos = from + (to − from)·e/1000, integer division truncating toward zero; at p = 1000 exactly to

crates.rows: the first three crates opened, one row each; later crates get no row; Gathered adds up every crate

probe.from: the dock's mend { free, paid, broke } (state.mjs dockKey), kept in Cargo's UI state from the dock until the report: free or broke (a break is mended free) reads strings.report.mendedFree, paid reads strings.report.mendedPaid with ⚡ and the plates paid for; no mend, no row. It is not in the save: a reload loses it, and the report then has no Probe row

world.from: the last walk crate opened (dev crates carry no lines)

reach.thresholds: r = explored/of: below 1/3 underThird; 1/3 to below 2/3 underTwoThirds; 2/3 to below 1 underAll; explored ≥ of all; of = 0 (a crate with no map) says nothing

notes.motion: Reduced motion (props.motion false; UI designer, 2026-10-10 02:29): every step is a cut to its end. crateIn: the crates stand in their places on the frame of the dock, hold 0. The opening keeps its pace and its hold (crates × 3000 + 200): one crate every 3000 ms, each step at its time as a cut, because each crate's words, materials and world turn are read in turn; the report shows at the end. A press that ends an event with `cut: true` also acts (habitat.json notes.cut); no event here cuts. With props.motion false the host sends events.opening once at 0 (ms and hold unchanged) and stages each step as props at its time, crate k from k·3000: sealed at 0, open at 200 (no opening slice), ribbon 500, counters at their new values 800, pod i in its well at 1200 + 150·i, turn 1650; the report at crates × 3000. The face only cuts.

crateIn.when: the Companion docks with crates while Cargo shows

byCrates.rule: the host sends whole ms: crates × 3000 + 180 and the hold 20 ms longer, for 1 to 9 crates (hold ≤ 30000, lvgl-switch §2.7); in play at most 3. With 10 or more (developer only) the event plays the first nine; the rest are taken in by openBay, the counters and turn reach their final values at the end

opening.focus: the room; no ring; no key moves it

crate.do: the dither (16 levels) from the bay, or from the crate before, to this crate closer: regions.crate sealed, the ribbon, the rack
the seal tag tears and the lid lifts: sealed → opening → open, its pods in their places
the ribbon shows this crate's words (a cut, no fade)
the counters tick this crate's materials (the top bar's own tick and flash)
each pod travels from the crate to its well (regions.travel), in well order; a pod with no free well stays in the crate
the world turn jumps to the crate's turn (the top bar's tick)

end.do: the dither back to the bay, empty, with the report card over it (state report)

focus.room: the ring on nothing: Cargo has no targets; ✓ does the bottom line's action, the pad does nothing
focus.held: while events.opening holds, the face moves no focus and sends no intent but room:<x> (kept by the host and dispatched when the hold ends), when the report shows. A Dock during the opening is kept by the host (by parity: two presses cancel) and acts when the hold ends, before a kept room key; it does not close the report card.
focus.report: while the report card shows, any key closes it and also does what it does: ✓ follows the bottom line, ← only closes it, the pad only closes it, a room key closes it and opens its section

confirm.bay: a crate ready to open (walk crates while docked, a ready sitting crate): the opening (events.opening); else nothing, no ✓ cap
confirm.report: See the new pod or See the new pods (strings.newPods): the jump to Pods (frame.json navigation.jumps); with no new pod, Done: the card closes

back.bay: Home, the ring on the Cargo module
back.report: closes the card: the bay, empty

keys.dock: the Caddy's Dock, a world event, never a Station key. Docked while the bay shows: the lid opens (a cut) and the crates slide in (events.crateIn). Lifted while the bay shows: the lid shuts (a cut). During the opening it waits until the report shows. No message plate: the bay, the top bar's Companion mark and the context line say it. A refused Dock shows its plate.

crates.when: a crate is ready to open: walk crates while docked, a ready sitting crate docked or away
crates.subject: strings.subjects.crates
crates.need: the most pressing notice after the crates (home.json strings.needs)

handoff.rule: a crate's pods land in the rack, the Station's six wells: Pods' collection shows them in the same wells, new until identified. ✓ See the new pods on the report jumps to Pods' collection with the ring on the pod that most needs the player; ← there reads Home. A pod with no free well waits in the bay (regions.waiting) and lands, oldest first, as a well frees

subjects.waitingOne: a pod waits for a well

ribbon.rule: the crate only, no digits; the ordinal counts walk crates only (first, second, third; past the third, later, never from play); every dev crate reads dev; the land's reach is on the report card

placeholders.crate-sealed-256x176: the bay's crate, a rugged field case: enamel body, deepTeal rubber corners, an orange seal tag
placeholders.crate-opening-384x256: the tag torn, the lid lifting
placeholders.crate-open-384x256: the lid off, its fitted cut-outs
placeholders.bay: 992×320 panel; the lid enamel with deepTeal seals
placeholders.icon-pod-16: the report's Pod icon, 16×16: a PH plate
placeholders.icon-shield-16: the report's Shield icon, 16×16: a PH plate, one per plate mended (a lost plate is not shown); never Home's 12×24 Shield placeholder
